notes.decision: Both forms construed as Lycopolitan present-I declarative formulas of teacher-disciple address: 'I am declaring/proclaiming (it/them) to you/to your souls.' The exact morphology is uncertain — ⲛⲉⲓⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ may = ⲛⲉⲓ̈- (pres I) + dat 2pl ⲧⲏⲛⲉ; ⲛⲉⲓ̈ⲉⲧⲟⲩ likely Pres I + 3pl object 'them.' Translated 'declare/proclaim' to fit the rhetorical context of revealing mysteries.

Read as Lycopolitan ⲛϥ-(ⲇⲓ)ⲁⲕⲣⲓⲛⲉ 'that he may discriminate/distinguish.' Greek loanword διακρίνειν, the technical verb for the dualist act of distinguishing the two substances of light and darkness. The doubled ⲁⲁ may reflect /διa-/ via vowel assimilation.

Both are Lycopolitan action-nouns formed with the ⲟ̄ⲓⲛ-/ⲟ̄ⲓ- nominalizing prefix (cf. ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ 'dissolution,' ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ†ⲟⲩⲱ 'raising' in glossary): 'his shining-forth' (ⲡⲣⲓⲉ — same root as ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance') and 'his setting' (ϩⲱⲧⲡ̄, said of the sun). The contrast preserves the active-emission semantics of ⲡⲣⲓⲉ per terminology guide.

Read as ⲥⲱⲧ + ⲛ̄ⲍⲱⲱⲩ 'draw themselves' (ⲥⲱⲧ akin to ⲥⲱⲕ 'pull, draw'; ⲭⲱⲩ as Lyc. reflex of reflexive ϩⲱⲟⲩ 'themselves,' cf. ⲍⲱⲱϩ noted in dialect entries). The creatures of flesh draw themselves out of sleep at sunrise.

ⲧⲟⲛⲱ = Lycopolitan ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raising' (per terminology guide must preserve vertical/upward semantics). The day-mystery IS named 'a great Raising-up' — the sun's morning re-emergence is correspondentially the cosmic raising of light. Capitalized to mark the technical Manichaean register.

Read as the directional infinitive ⲁ-ϣⲁⲣϣⲣ̄, with ϣⲁⲣϣⲣ̄/ϣⲣ̄ϣⲣ̄ a reduplicated form related to the scattering/breaking root underlying ⲭⲣⲁⲣⲁⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'scattered forth' in the glossary. In Manichaean correspondential terms, humans coming forth at dawn 'scatter upon' (= work, cut, harvest) the Cross of Light — Jesus patibilis enduring suffering through their daily activity.

ⲡⲧⲏϩ from ⲧⲱϩ 'mix, join, match' substantivized = 'the matching, the corresponding-to.' The construction ⲉⲣⲉ ⲡⲉⲓ̈ ⲡⲧⲏϩ ⲁ- = 'this matches/corresponds to.' Standard Manichaean correspondential identifier.
